# PR #1784: Patch: the AI keeps its own position switches in the beam, so a losing attacker can stand down

Closes #1759

## What changed and why

The AI almost never moved its own units to Defense Position. Position switches are the last tier of `in_move_order`, and `expand` keeps only the first `branching` moves (6) below the root. So on a busy board every switch was cut before the AI simulated it. The opponent the AI imagines has no such limit: it tries up to `AI_REPLY.defense_switches` ATK→DEF switches on every reply step.

- **`crates/ai/src/config.rs`**: a new named constant `AI_SEARCH.position_switches: 2` (K).
- **`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`**: a new `stands_down(state, action)`. It is true for a `SwitchPosition` that moves a unit from Attack to Defense, but only when some enemy unit would kill that unit and survive (`kills_and_survives`), i.e. the unit cannot win its next fight. It reads only public state: positions, attack and health through `unit_view` and `active_units_of`.
- **`crates/ai/src/search.rs`**: after the `width` cut, `expand` adds back the first K stand-downs that the cut dropped, then End Turn as before.
  - A stand-down the kept moves already hold is not added twice.
  - Each level therefore has at most `width + K + 1` children.
  - Switches back to Attack, and switches of units no enemy would beat, stay where the cut leaves them.
- **Spec**:
  - New ruling `spec/rulings/R1759000.md`, proven in `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`.
  - `R1171001` now notes the amendment: the policy prior still only re-sorts the kept moves.
  - `spec/11-rulings.md` has a summary entry, and `spec/INDEX.md` was regenerated.
- **`crates/ai/README.md`**: the search paragraph now describes the kept stand-downs.
- **`crates/server/tests/fixtures/practice-claim.json`**: re-recorded. The practice AI now takes a different line in this game: one extra `activate`, and the last attack replaces End Turn.

## Tests

- **Puzzle** `unused_attacker_facing_a_bigger_enemy_ends_in_defense_position` (`tests/ai/puzzles.rs`): Mr. Vanilla (4/4) faces the Archivist (4/5). In Attack it dies in the next fight; Defense's +1 Armor keeps it alive. The AI ends its turn with it in Defense.
- **Expansion tests** in `tests/ai/search.rs`:
  - stand-downs survive the cut up to K;
  - the kept ones are the first the cut dropped (`r1759000_the_kept_stand_downs_are_the_first_the_cut_left_out`);
  - a unit no enemy would beat is not stood down.
- **Policy test**: the `todays` helper in `tests/ai/policy.rs` now matches the new `expand`, so `r1171001_off_or_null_the_order_is_today_s` still compares like with like.

What I ran in this pass, all passing:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`: exit 0, and `apps/web/src/wire/` is unchanged
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: 1123 rulings, ok
- `cargo jackioh catalog check`: ok
- `cargo jackioh patches check`: ok

**Gate:** I did not rerun `cargo jackioh gate` in this pass, because this pass changed only one test assertion. Pass 2 recorded the smoke gate as clean (random 19/20, greedy 20/20, hard-vs-easy 16/20 with 16 needed). Hard-vs-easy sits exactly on its floor, so watch it on the daily `gate --full`.

## Decisions

- **Only real stand-downs are kept**, not every switch. Keeping any switch also kept switches of units nobody threatened, and that dropped hard-vs-easy to 15/20, below its floor. Requiring an enemy that would kill the unit and survive matches the issue's wording ("cannot win its next fight") and brought the gate back to 16/20.
- **K counts the stand-downs the cut dropped**, not all stand-downs, so one already in the kept moves does not use up a slot.
- **`AI_EVAL.position_grants` stays 0.0.** The issue offered a nonzero value as optional, but a weight change needs gate evidence. The lookahead already sees that the unit in Defense survives, so the puzzle passes without it.
- **No change to the order of `in_move_order`.** The plan's ATK→DEF-first sort is unnecessary, because the cut-and-add-back step already picks stand-downs in candidate order.

## Review findings

- **blocking, `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs:518`: clippy `int_plus_one` failed on HEAD.** The finding held. I changed `assert!(stand_downs.len() >= 1 + kept)` to `assert!(stand_downs.len() > kept)`, which means the same thing. Workspace clippy with `-D warnings` now passes, so the `clippy` check this change turned red is fixed.

# #1759: Patch: the AI keeps its own position switches in the beam, so a losing attacker can stand down
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In practice the AI almost never moves one of its units to Defense Position on its own turn — even when that unit cannot win its next fight and Defense would keep it alive (Defense grants Taunt and +1 Armor). Its own suggestion machinery tries position switches dead last and usually discards them before simulating a single one, while the opponent it imagines does get to try them. After the change the AI can choose to stand a unit down, the way a real player does.

## Why

`in_move_order` puts every `SwitchPosition` in the last tier — behind hero attacks, trades, plays, powers, activates, answers and other attacks (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:592-633`), and `expand` truncates to `branching: 6` below the root (`crates/ai/src/search.rs:104-115`), so a mid-line switch survives only when fewer than six earlier-tier moves exist. The asymmetry is sharp: the imagined opponent gets up to `AI_REPLY.defense_switches: 4` explicit ATK→DEF trials every reply step (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:362-379`, `config.rs:730`), while the seat's own turn may hold none. `position_grants: 0.0` (`config.rs:407`) compounds it — the static eval reads Defense's Taunt/+1 Armor as roughly nothing (`evaluate.rs:128-148`), so a switch looks like a pure attack loss. `lethal_moves` already recognizes that switches matter for Deft (`lethal.rs:71-80`). Concrete misplay: the AI ends its turn with an unused attacker in Attack facing a bigger enemy unit; a real player parks it in Defense and it survives — the AI's unit dies.

## Proposal

Append up to K `SwitchPosition` actions after `expand`'s truncation, the way `EndTurn` is preserved (`search.rs:111-114`), optionally with a modest nonzero `position_grants` screen so the eval reads Defense's defensive value. A puzzle test asserts the switch is chosen on a losing-Attack board.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/search.rs` (`expand`), `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` (tier ordering), `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (`AI_SEARCH`, `position_grants`); a puzzle under `crates/ai/tests/ai/`; measured by `cargo jackioh gate`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A named puzzle: an unused attacker facing a bigger enemy ends in Defense Position
- [ ] Switches survive truncation without unbounded branching (K is a named constant)
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` stays clean at smoke size
- [ ] No hidden-information read — the switch logic uses only what the seat may see

## Size and risks

Small — roughly 30-60 lines plus a puzzle. The risk is decision time in fat states, bounded by K and measured against the decision budget; a weight change needs gate evidence, not a hunch.

# #1759: Patch: the AI keeps its own position switches in the beam, so a losing attacker can stand down
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In practice the AI almost never moves one of its units to Defense Position on its own turn — even when that unit cannot win its next fight and Defense would keep it alive (Defense grants Taunt and +1 Armor). Its own suggestion machinery tries position switches dead last and usually discards them before simulating a single one, while the opponent it imagines does get to try them. After the change the AI can choose to stand a unit down, the way a real player does.

## Why

`in_move_order` puts every `SwitchPosition` in the last tier — behind hero attacks, trades, plays, powers, activates, answers and other attacks (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:592-633`), and `expand` truncates to `branching: 6` below the root (`crates/ai/src/search.rs:104-115`), so a mid-line switch survives only when fewer than six earlier-tier moves exist. The asymmetry is sharp: the imagined opponent gets up to `AI_REPLY.defense_switches: 4` explicit ATK→DEF trials every reply step (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:362-379`, `config.rs:730`), while the seat's own turn may hold none. `position_grants: 0.0` (`config.rs:407`) compounds it — the static eval reads Defense's Taunt/+1 Armor as roughly nothing (`evaluate.rs:128-148`), so a switch looks like a pure attack loss. `lethal_moves` already recognizes that switches matter for Deft (`lethal.rs:71-80`). Concrete misplay: the AI ends its turn with an unused attacker in Attack facing a bigger enemy unit; a real player parks it in Defense and it survives — the AI's unit dies.

## Proposal

Append up to K `SwitchPosition` actions after `expand`'s truncation, the way `EndTurn` is preserved (`search.rs:111-114`), optionally with a modest nonzero `position_grants` screen so the eval reads Defense's defensive value. A puzzle test asserts the switch is chosen on a losing-Attack board.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/search.rs` (`expand`), `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` (tier ordering), `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (`AI_SEARCH`, `position_grants`); a puzzle under `crates/ai/tests/ai/`; measured by `cargo jackioh gate`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A named puzzle: an unused attacker facing a bigger enemy ends in Defense Position
- [ ] Switches survive truncation without unbounded branching (K is a named constant)
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` stays clean at smoke size
- [ ] No hidden-information read — the switch logic uses only what the seat may see

## Size and risks

Small — roughly 30-60 lines plus a puzzle. The risk is decision time in fat states, bounded by K and measured against the decision budget; a weight change needs gate evidence, not a hunch.
